card.title: Symbol of Office
card.instruction: Choose one symbol, privilege, or position and treat control of it as proof of legitimate authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm wearing the barbecue apron. I decide when the burgers turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you should respect its office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Put it on, and you can tell me to turn them. Until then, leave my burgers alone.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats the worn apron as authority, A3 distinguishes its office from ownership, and A5 accepts transfer only once B actually wears it.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's ownership claim informs A3's office reply; B4's take-it-back proposal causes A5's wearer-based transfer condition.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 plausibly reclaim personal property rather than debating an abstract institution.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's reclamation to specify when commands will change hands, preserving A's present burger control.

specificity.evidence: A1 names the apron, barbecue and burger timing; B2 identifies its actual owner.
